title: regional-quiet-window-prober-and-tenant-cooldown-agent
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight regional probing agent and a transient tenant cooldown coordinator to reduce noisy failovers during short-lived regional load spikes. Motivation: Recent incident SUP-8773 showed a thundering reopen pattern where regions flipped between healthy and degraded for short windows (~30-90s), causing tenant-level eviction oscillation and unnecessary cross-region failovers. The goal is to provide a short, observable 'quiet window' probe that: 1) distinguishes transient noise from stable degradation, 2) applies a tenant-scoped cooldown to avoid immediate re-eviction/reinstate churn, and 3) emits detailed telemetry for post-incident analysis. Changes: - Add regional probe loop (runtime/region/prober) that performs low-overhead health probes tied to the soft-failover decision path. Probes run at a configurable cadence and calculate a transientness score based on recent latency/error samples. - Introduce tenant cooldown agent (orchestrator/cooldown) that tracks per-tenant cooldown epochs, prevents reinstates for N seconds after a revert, and backs off re-eligible attempts with exponential jitter. - Wire probe score into the SLO enforcer so that transient-probe=high will prefer a soft-shed action over immediate regional failover. - Telemetry: new metrics (region_probe_score, tenant_cooldown_remaining, probe_sample_histogram) plus debug traces for decision branches. - Config: feature flag runtime.feature.regional_quiet_window + config knobs for cadence, window_size, score_threshold, cooldown_base_seconds. Backwards compatibility: feature is off by default and default cooldown is conservative (30s). Rolling upgrade safe: probe agent tolerates missing config and will no-op. Tests & CI: included unit tests for score calc and tenant cooldown state machine, integration test that simulates a transient spike and verifies no cross-region failover. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for probe scoring - [x] Integration test for transient spike behavior - [x] Add metrics and logs - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Documentation snippet in docs/reliability/quiet-window.md - [x] Observability dashboard draft (console/dashboards/quiet-window.json) Related: SUP-8773, ENG-4129, ENG-4132, earlier experiments in pr-731210 (surge-moderation).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice minimal approach. Two requests: make the default cooldown configurable by release and add an admin override API for immediate tenant restore.
Maya Chen (author): Added cooldown config and admin /internal/tenants/:id/restore override behind ops-only auth. See orchestrator/cooldown/agent.go + tests. PTAL.
Priya Shah: The score calculation looks plausible but please add a short comment describing sensitivity to sample size; currently small windows can be noisy.
Maya Chen (author): Expanded comments and bumped minimum sample count to 5 to avoid single-sample flips. Updated unit tests to cover min sample case.
Cameron Li: CI initially failed on lint (gofmt) and flaky integration timing. Suggestions: relax integration timing assertions and run go fmt. Fixed in commit 0d1e2f.
Priya Shah: Approved after changes. Diego Alvarez: Approved. Merged by Maya Chen.
release_notes:
- Add regional quiet-window probing to reduce transient reopen oscillations
- Introduce tenant cooldown to avoid immediate re-eviction churn
- New metrics for probe score and tenant cooldown state
- Feature flag runtime.feature.regional_quiet_window (off by default)
notes: Operational notes: Enable feature behind canary for a subset of regions. Start with cooldown_base_seconds=30 and cadence=10s. Monitor region_probe_score and tenant_cooldown_remaining. If too conservative, lower cooldown; if too permissive, raise threshold. Incident SUP-8773 follow-up: this should prevent the immediate symptom but team should still investigate root cause of transient latency bursts (network/egress).
